baseline.note: Calibrated to the 2026Q1 ledger; Taylor rule; passive (Bohn) fiscal reaction; no AI adoption.

credit_boom.note: Dalio's short-term debt cycle: lending standards loosen at quarters 8 and 12, leverage targets extrapolate income growth, the boom ends in debt-service stress and write-offs.

baseline_high_capital_mpc.note: Reference run for the high-capital-MPC hike: same parameters, no shock.

dark_output_captured.note: AI adoption to 100%; displaced wage bill captured as profits (sigma = 1). Real capacity rises 10% unmeasured.

dark_output_passthrough.note: AI adoption to 100%; displaced wage bill passed through as lower prices (sigma = 0).

dark_output_mixed.note: AI adoption to 100%; half captured, half passed through.

dark_output_fiscal_offset.note: As 'mixed', but with an active fiscal stabilizer (the MMT prescription).

mosler_zirp_fiscal.note: Policy rate permanently zero; fiscal policy does the stabilizing.

rate_hike_300bp.note: A 3pp policy-rate shock at quarter 20, decaying; conventional channels only (MPC out of capital income = 0.3).

rate_hike_300bp_cost_channel.note: Same hike, plus Mosler's cost channel: inflation responds to the change in loan rates.

rate_hike_300bp_high_capital_mpc.note: Same hike, with a higher MPC out of interest and dividends (0.6): the sign of rate policy flips. Compare against baseline_high_capital_mpc, not baseline.

fiscal_dominance.note: No fiscal reaction to debt, higher MPC out of capital income, Taylor rule: the interest-income spiral (Sargent-Wallace / Dalio's endgame). Diverges by design.
